title: weinmannia pubescens var. popayanensis
intro: Weinmannia pubescens var. popayanensis, commonly known as the 'Canelo' or 'Quina', is a plant species native to the Andean region, which belongs to the family Cunoniaceae. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health conditions, such as digestive issues, fever, and respiratory problems, due to its potential health benefits. The therapeutic actions of Canelo include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant effects, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and coumarins. Research on Canelo has identified its potential to support immune function, reduce oxidative stress, and exhibit antiviral properties, highlighting its promise as a valuable natural remedy.
